mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) has a negative causal relationship with S&P 500 forward returns: each 1 percentage point decrease in FEDFUNDS predicts a positive 20-day return due to reduced discount rates for equity valuations and increased liquidity, holding all else constant.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 2.0%, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in unemployment rate above 6.0% (UNRATE > 6.0) signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 6.0%, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: The interaction between low monetary policy rates (FEDFUNDS < 2.0) and weak residential demand (RSAFS < 350000) signals recessionary expectations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as investors price in prolonged economic weakness.
failure_condition: The interaction signal fails to predict negative returns in more than 60% of cases when FEDFUNDS < 2.0 AND RSAFS < 350000, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production (INDPRO < 110.0) during recessionary regimes signals manufacturing contraction that reduces corporate profits, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO < 110.0 during recession, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Strong residential sales (RSAFS > 375000) indicate robust consumer demand and economic activity, supporting corporate earnings growth and producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when RSAFS exceeds 375000, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 2.0% (FEDFUNDS < 2.0) signals aggressive monetary easing that initially boosts equity valuations through lower discount rates, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 2.0%, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: The interaction between high unemployment (UNRATE > 6.0) and weak residential demand (RSAFS < 350000) amplifies recessionary fears, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending collapses.
failure_condition: The interaction signal fails to predict negative returns in more than 60% of cases when UNRATE > 6.0 AND RSAFS < 350000, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During early recession regimes (UNRATE > 6.0 and declining GDP), the S&P 500 experiences negative forward returns as unemployment-driven income losses suppress consumer spending and corporate margins.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE > 6.0 during early recession, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
